feat(zshrc): auto-enable proxy on Bunnings machines when VPN connected

Conditionally runs proxy-on when shell starts if:
1. Hostname starts with "BUN" (Bunnings machine)
2. GlobalProtect process is running (VPN connected)

This ensures NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS is set automatically for Claude Code
and other Node.js tools behind the corporate SSL-inspecting proxy.

refactor(setup): consolidate bootstrap.sh + install.sh into unified setup.sh

Merge the 7-phase installer (bootstrap.sh) and config subcommands
(install.sh) into a single entry point. setup.sh now supports both
full install (phases 0-6 with checkpoint/resume) and subcommands
(symlinks, prefs, status, verify). Phase 6 added for configuration.

Update all references in README.md, verify_install.sh,
defaults.server.sh, brew_remote_bundle.sh, and CHEZMOI_EVALUATION.md.
Also fix stale master->main branch ref in brew_remote_bundle.sh.

fix(brew): move codex and codexbar to shared casks

Both are CLI tools that work on headless servers — no reason to gate
them behind the desktop profile. Also updates MCP runner references
to use published npm packages.

refactor(macos): consolidate preferences into config/macos/

Move macOS preferences from bin/system/macos/ to config/macos/defaults.common.sh,
fixing the sudo anti-pattern where all user-domain `defaults write` calls incorrectly
used sudo. Now follows Mathias Bynens' pattern: no sudo for user domains, direct
defaults write calls organized by section.

New desktop-dev settings: trackpad tap-to-click, zero-delay dock autohide, disabled
window animations, Finder status bar, screenshots to ~/Screenshots, chflags nohidden
~/Library, network BrowseAllInterfaces.

New server settings: systemsetup -setrestartfreeze, login window hostname display,
disabled automatic updates (server controls its own reboots).

Delete 6 legacy files: broken wrappers with bad quoting, dead genie/ references.

fix(clt): handle Tahoe softwareupdate label format

macOS Tahoe 26.x changed softwareupdate output format from
"* Command Line Tools..." to "Label: Command Line Tools...".
The sed pipeline now strips both prefixes. Also restructured the
install flow to verify CLT actually installed after softwareupdate
before falling back to xcode-select --install, since softwareupdate
can silently fail with exit code 0.

fix(setup): install Xcode CLT before git clone

setup.sh tries to git clone the dotfiles repo, but git requires
Xcode Command Line Tools. Previously this would fail on a fresh Mac
since CLT wasn't installed until bootstrap.sh Phase 1 ran (which
happens after cloning). Now setup.sh installs CLT non-interactively
via softwareupdate before attempting the clone.

fix(bootstrap): automate Xcode CLT install without GUI dialog

Use softwareupdate CLI to install Command Line Tools non-interactively,
enabling fully automated setup over SSH without needing to click a dialog.
Falls back to xcode-select --install if softwareupdate can't find the package.

fix(verify): improve DX for verification script

- Source Homebrew shellenv at start of verify script (fixes PATH issue)
- Remove set -e to allow all checks to run even if some fail
- Use $((x + 1)) instead of ((x++)) for safer arithmetic
- verify() now returns 0 to continue checking after failures
- setup.sh now uses || true so verification doesn't fail the install
- Add clear success banner at end of setup

This ensures the install appears successful when it is, with
verification being informational rather than causing false failures.

fix(symlinks): add --force flag for non-interactive mode

- Add --force flag to replace existing files/dirs without prompting
- Detect non-interactive mode (stdin not a terminal) and skip prompts
- In force mode, backup existing files before replacing
- install.sh now uses --force when running non-interactively

Fixes: install.sh failing in curl | bash scenarios when .config exists

chore(zsh): update plugin paths for extracted plugins

Point biome-runner, bun-runner, tsc-runner to side-quest-plugins repo.

fix(brew): use HOMEBREW_ prefix for env vars in Brewfile

Homebrew filters out non-HOMEBREW_ prefixed environment variables
before evaluating Brewfile Ruby context for security/isolation.

Changed DOTFILES_PROFILE to HOMEBREW_DOTFILES_PROFILE so profile
conditionals work correctly (server vs desktop).

Fixes: Desktop apps being installed on server profile

docs: add Chezmoi migration evaluation

Document pros/cons of migrating to Chezmoi for dotfiles management.
Conclusion: not worth migrating now, revisit if adding more machines
or needing secrets encryption.

refactor(brew): consolidate Brewfiles with Ruby conditionals

Replace 3 separate Brewfiles (common, desktop, server) with a single
unified Brewfile that uses Ruby conditionals for profile-specific packages.

Usage: DOTFILES_PROFILE=server brew bundle --file=config/brew/Brewfile

Benefits:
- Single source of truth for all packages
- No file generation/concatenation needed
- Easier to see what differs between profiles
- Standard Homebrew pattern for multi-machine setups

feat(bootstrap): add machine profiles with phased installation

Implement modular dotfiles bootstrap supporting desktop (MacBook Pro)
and server (Mac Mini) profiles with 7-phase architecture and AI rescue.

New files:
- config/brew/Brewfile.common: shared CLI tools for all profiles
- config/brew/Brewfile.desktop: desktop GUI apps (Slack, VS Code, etc.)
- config/brew/Brewfile.server: server-specific (OrbStack, Ollama)
- config/macos/defaults.server.sh: server macOS settings (pmset, SSH, firewall)
- verify_install.sh: post-installation verification script

Modified:
- setup.sh: --server/--desktop flags, curl pipe safety, profile persistence
- bootstrap.sh: 7-phase architecture with checkpoint/resume support
- install.sh: profile-aware preferences, server-specific settings

Usage:
  curl ... | bash -s -- --desktop  # MacBook Pro
  curl ... | bash -s -- --server   # Mac Mini headless
  ./bootstrap.sh --resume          # Resume from failure

feat(tmux): enhance worktree scripts with auto-install and bug fixes

Worktree creation (worktree-ai.sh):
- Add package manager detection (bun > yarn > pnpm > npm)
- Auto-run install with non-interactive flags (--frozen-lockfile)
- Switch Node version via fnm/nvm before install
- Copy untracked files (.env, .claude, CLAUDE.md, *.kit) to new worktrees
- Bootstrap existing worktrees on attach (copy files, install if stale)
- Support packageManager field (corepack) and warn on conflicting lock files
- Add timeout wrapper and command existence checks

Bug fixes:
- Check git exit codes in ensure_worktree
- Replace dots with hyphens in session names (fixes tmux targeting)
- Use Unit Separator delimiter instead of tilde (path-safe)
- Validate destination exists before copy operations
- Query pane-base-index instead of hardcoding
- Suppress cp output pollution

Worktree deletion (worktree-delete.sh):
- Multi-select UX with TAB in fzf picker
- Two-step flow: delete worktrees first, then optionally branches
- Session kill with verification loop (no race condition)
- Show branch status (pristine/merged/N ahead)
- Quote $delete_flag variable

Also removes debug wrapper scripts and simplifies tmux bindings.

feat(tmux): show all branches as bases for new worktrees

New picker flow:
- [+] Create new branch (from HEAD)
- Attach to Worktree - existing worktrees
- New branch from Local - all local branches as bases
- New branch from Remote - all remote branches as bases

When selecting a local/remote branch, prompts for new branch name
then creates worktree with new branch from that base.

fix(tmux): show all remote branches regardless of merge status

--no-merged is relative to current branch, which gives different
results depending on which worktree you're in. Remove it to show
all remote branches consistently.
fix(tmux): fetch remotes before listing branches in worktree-ai

fix(tmux): use realpath in tx to avoid fnm chpwd hook pollution

When resolving relative paths, `cd && pwd` triggers zsh's chpwd hook,
which runs fnm's auto-version-switch that outputs warnings to stdout.
This polluted the captured path with extra lines, causing tmuxinator
to fail with YAML parsing errors.

Using `realpath` instead avoids directory changes entirely, so no
shell hooks fire and the path resolution stays clean.
